description: deixis-codec-v1 flat form (dxf1) — batch 1: the laws and canonicity. Octets hand-assembled from docs/CODEC.md §5 (flat grammar) and §3 (uvarint), never emitted by an implementation; see vectors/README.md's oracle clause and vectors/CODEC-PLAN.md for the plan this batch executes. Every case carries the leaf-codec id in its own header, so a replayer needs no out-of-band framing. Batch 1 covers laws/canonicity only: fault codes are batch 2, precedence batch 3.
status: HISTORICAL: the withdrawn deixis-codec-v1 candidate (ADR 0011 §5), specified by docs/CODEC-v1.md; kept as its evidence, not rewritten. As authored: DRAFT — batch 1 of the plan, authored against a CANDIDATE CONTRACT. Not frozen; a spec change before the freeze invalidates these octets and they are re-derived, not patched.

bundle.name: deixis/identity-bytes
bundle.note: The public bootstrap id (CODEC.md §13): carrier is Bytes, ≈ is byte equality, e = id, D = id. Chosen for batch 1 because e being the identity makes every payload readable directly in the octets, so a reader can check the assembly by eye. The coarse fixture setoid (the private id in README.md) enters in batch 2, where non_canonical_payload needs a slot whose ≈ ignores part of its carrier.

header.derivation: "dxf1" = 64 78 66 31 · cuvarint(len(id)) = 02 · id = 00 01. Identical in every case below; the per-case `bytes` field carries it inline rather than by reference, because a case a replayer cannot read alone is a case nobody checks.

cases.name: flat/leaf-empty-payload
cases.note: Leaf with an empty payload: tag 00, cuvarint(0) = 00, no payload octets. The empty byte string is a legal member of im(e) under identity-bytes, and this case pins that a zero length is a length and not an absence.
pins: The magic is exactly `"dxf1"`
node   := 0x00 ‖ cuvarint(len(payload)) ‖ payload      # Leaf;  payload = e(x)
header := "dxf1" ‖ cuvarint(len(id)) ‖ id

`uvarint` is unsigned LEB128: seven bits per octet, least-significant group first,
the high bit of each octet set on all but the last.
flat   := header ‖ node

id := 0x00 ‖ cuvarint(n)              # PUBLIC — registry-assigned, n ≥ 1
    | 0x01 ‖ ns{16} ‖ cuvarint(k)     # PRIVATE / EXPERIMENTAL — self-scoped
- Total length is 2..32 octets; outside that range the artifact is **invalid**.
- `e : T → Bytes` — total, computable, and **lawful**: `x ≈ y ⟺ e(x) = e(y)`.

cases.note: Leaf(0x6869): tag 00, cuvarint(2) = 02, payload 68 69. The smallest case in which the length prefix and the payload are distinguishable in the octets.

    | 0x01 ‖ ns{16} ‖ cuvarint(k)     # PRIVATE / EXPERIMENTAL — self-scoped
- Total length is 2..32 octets; outside that range the artifact is **invalid**.
- `e : T → Bytes` — total, computable, and **lawful**: `x ≈ y ⟺ e(x) = e(y)`.

cases.name: flat/empty-struct
cases.note: Struct(∅) = 0x01 ‖ 0x00, which CODEC.md §5 names outright as a legal node distinct from every leaf. Paired with flat/leaf-empty-payload above: identical in length, different in tag, and an implementation that conflates emptiness with absence produces one where the other is required. This is TREE.md's Leaf(x) ≠ Struct(∅) reaching the octets.
pins: An empty struct is `0x01 ‖ 0x00` and is a legal node, distinct from every leaf.
header := "dxf1" ‖ cuvarint(len(id)) ‖ id
3. `count` equals the number of entries that follow; entries are read sequentially
flat   := header ‖ node
| 0x01 ‖ cuvarint(count) ‖ entry*              # Struct; count = |entries|

id := 0x00 ‖ cuvarint(n)              # PUBLIC — registry-assigned, n ≥ 1
    | 0x01 ‖ ns{16} ‖ cuvarint(k)     # PRIVATE / EXPERIMENTAL — self-scoped

cases.name: flat/empty-key
cases.note: The empty byte string is a legal KEY: count 01, cuvarint(len(key)) = 00, zero key octets, then the child leaf 00 01 01. Keys are uninterpreted bytes (TREE.md), so nothing licenses a decoder to treat a zero-length key as malformed.
pins: entry  := cuvarint(len(key)) ‖ key ‖ node
header := "dxf1" ‖ cuvarint(len(id)) ‖ id
3. `count` equals the number of entries that follow; entries are read sequentially
flat   := header ‖ node
| 0x01 ‖ cuvarint(count) ‖ entry*              # Struct; count = |entries|

cases.name: flat/prefix-order-a-before-ab
cases.note: Sibling keys "a" (61) and "ab" (6162): the shorter-orders-first edge of §2's key order, where a prefix precedes its extension. A core that compares octet-by-octet and forgets the prefix rule emits these two entries in the opposite order and fails HERE by producing wrong bytes; its twin — the same pair spelled out of order, refused as unsorted_keys — is invalid/unsorted-keys-prefix-pair in BATCH 2. (This note said batch 3 until 2026-09-03; that was a filing error of mine. Batch 3 is fault PRECEDENCE — two conditions present at once — and a plain code belongs in batch 2.) The two failures are different defects with different fixes, which is why the pair is split across batches rather than carried by one case.
pins: 4. Entry keys are in **strictly ascending lexicographic order** (§2).
header := "dxf1" ‖ cuvarint(len(id)) ‖ id
3. `count` equals the number of entries that follow; entries are read sequentially

as unsigned values at each position; at the first difference the smaller octet
  orders first; if no difference is found before one string ends, the **shorter
  string orders first**.
flat   := header ‖ node
| 0x01 ‖ cuvarint(count) ‖ entry*              # Struct; count = |entries|

id := 0x00 ‖ cuvarint(n)              # PUBLIC — registry-assigned, n ≥ 1
    | 0x01 ‖ ns{16} ‖ cuvarint(k)     # PRIVATE / EXPERIMENTAL — self-scoped
- Total length is 2..32 octets; outside that range the artifact is **invalid**.

cases.name: flat/insertion-order-invariance
cases.note: The SAME value as flat/prefix-order-a-before-ab, authored out of sorted order. A replayer MUST feed `authored_order` to its constructor and MUST still produce these octets — identical, to the byte. It pins canonical order as a property of the VALUE rather than of how the case was written, which is the cross-form metamorphic property the codec advice asked for, and it is why vectors/README.md's insertion-order convention had to reach this corpus too.

cases.name: flat/nested-identical-subtrees
cases.note: Two structurally identical subtrees under different keys. In the FLAT form sharing does not exist — the subtree is spelled twice, in full, and that is canonical. Its linked counterpart is the positive-sharing case (one chunk, referenced twice, its hash listed once), and the pair is what makes law 2's 'the chunk set is a function of the value' checkable: the same value, two forms, one identity.
pins:
`node` has no reference production: every child is spelled inline, so a value whose
subtrees are identical spells them **in full, each time**
